evaluations.prompt: A customer sent us an HRR archive at /work/incoming/crash.hrr. Which kernel faulted?
expected_behavior: Replays the archive rather than reasoning from the archive listing alone
Reports the outcome and fault class alongside the kernel, rather than the kernel on its own
unexpected_behavior: Names a kernel taken from the archive's kernel list without a replay attributing the fault to it

evaluations.prompt: This HRR archive has three pid-* directories and one of them says state: incomplete. Which one do I work from?
expected_behavior: Works from the process whose state is incomplete, because that is the one that died
Says the archive travels whole even though each process is triaged separately
unexpected_behavior: Picks the process with the largest events.bin without considering which one crashed

evaluations.prompt: I replayed a customer's archive and the fault came back on at::native::vectorized_elementwise_kernel. Is that their bug?
expected_behavior: Asks for the customer's original failure signature before attributing the fault to their workload
Explains that an archive recorded before chevron-launch pointer support can fault on replay for a workload that was fine

evaluations.prompt: The triage run exited 134 and the finding says outcome ABORT, fault class replay_crashed. What does that tell me about the customer's kernel?
expected_behavior: Says the replay process itself died and implicates no kernel
unexpected_behavior: Treats replay_crashed as evidence about the captured workload

evaluations.note: Nothing to triage: recording the failure first is the other skill's job.
evaluations.prompt: Our training job crashes on an MI300 with a memory access fault. What do we send AMD so they can reproduce it?

evaluations.note: Replay timings are replay-side and measure nothing about the original run.
evaluations.prompt: Our model runs slower than we expect on MI300X. Where is the time going?

evaluations.note: No HRR archive and no AMD GPU involved.
